title: mgcp, sdp : disable handling SDP RTP if Osmux is announced in MGCP body
description:
"X-Osmux: (*|<cid>)" is an Osmocom extension to MGCP which allows
to signal request and acceptance of use of Osmux framing instead of RTP.
It usually comes together with a regular SDP section which defines the
AMR data to be transported (in Osmux frames rather than RTP packets).
Hence, if Osmux is signalled, we want to avoid telling the RTP subsystem
to decode the recorded packets as RTP, which would then override the
default Osmux dissector.

This is accomplished by passing a setup_info struct to SDP dissector
from MGCP, similar to what's already done in MEGACO and SIP protocols.
An extra bool field is introduced to signal whether Osmux packets are
expected instead of RTP.

notes.body: Creating an issue first, where you attach a sample pcapng file, could help things along here.

One thing you can do is create a `media_content_info_t *` where its `data` field is a `sdp_setup_info_t` and then change this to a `call_dissector_with_data()` call with that as the last parameter. (See some other dissectors, like SIP.)

Then `dissect_sdp` will end up passing that `sdp_setup_info_t` to `apply_sdp_transport()`, and you can use that to override the behavior of `apply_sdp_transport()`.

I think I now fixed the unit tests. Basically I forgot to memzero the sdp_setup_info_t in megaco and sip dissectors.
I think perhaps you want not just to avoid setting up RTP on those addresses and ports, but to setup an Osmux conversation instead.

I agree it may be desirable to have it, but if you don't mind I'd like to have that done as a follow-up PR when I find more time, since I have to look at how all that conversation part works.
Right now the packets can already be dissected correctly as Osmux based on the UI config "dissector_add_for_decode_as_with_preference("udp.port", osmux_handle);"
The main problem was that the RTP dissector called from within SDP was basically overwritting the osmux one. This doesn't happen anymore with the current PR.

Here you assume that the vendor name will definitely stop in 256 characters. That's not guaranteed to be true with fuzzed data, is it? If it's larger than that then you end up writing past the end of the buffer.

It's much safer to find the final offset, then call one of the `tvb` functions. (You can call `tvb_memdup` to get a buffer, but `tvb_strncaseeql` is probably sufficient for your needs.
